subject: botany_2
question_text: Define RQ. Write a short note on RQ.

mark_split.label: Why it never exceeds one for fats

verification.note: Sourced from "Sr. Botany — My Baby Bullet-Q" (Sri Publishers, STAR-Q Pass Track), book p.52, printed question 167. Botany-II holds only ONE source book: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no Telangana Botany-II board paper is in the corpus, so the two-book union check and the board back-test are BOTH structurally impossible for this card — "not checked" does NOT mean "checked and clean". Run both the moment a second source or a real paper arrives. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. BOOK ERROR, corrected on this card: under the correct formula (CO2 evolved over O2 consumed) the guide's own legend reads "A - stands for volume of CO2 ABSORBED during respiration. B - stands for volume of O2 LIBERATED during respiration." Both are reversed, and they contradict the formula printed two lines above them. Respiration takes O2 IN and gives CO2 OUT.

insider_note: RQ is a ratio with a direction. Carbon dioxide is on top because it comes OUT; oxygen is underneath because it goes IN. Getting that the wrong way round inverts every value.

steps.label: Definition and formula
steps.margin_note: Definition then formula. The direction of each gas is the mark.
lines: The RESPIRATORY QUOTIENT (RQ) is the ratio of
the volume of CO2 GIVEN OUT to the volume of
O2 TAKEN IN, in a given time at standard
steps.why: Different foods need different amounts of oxygen for the carbon dioxide they release, so the ratio identifies which food is being respired.
common_mistakes: Putting oxygen on top. CO2 given out is the NUMERATOR; O2 taken in is the denominator.
Writing 'CO2 absorbed' and 'O2 liberated'. Respiration takes oxygen IN and gives carbon dioxide OUT. The guide's own legend reverses both.
steps.memory_tip: Out over in: carbon dioxide out on top, oxygen in underneath.

steps.label: What the value tells you
steps.margin_note: Three cases, one line each. This mark is a list and should not be rushed.
lines: The value of RQ identifies the respiratory
If RQ = 1, CARBOHYDRATES are being used.
If RQ is LESS than 1, FATS are being used.
If RQ is MORE than 1, ORGANIC ACIDS are being
steps.why: A carbohydrate already carries as much oxygen as it needs, so it uses exactly as much oxygen as the carbon dioxide it gives out, and its RQ is exactly one.
common_mistakes: Saying fats give an RQ above 1. Fats give LESS than 1 because they need extra oxygen.
Leaving out organic acids. All three cases are asked for.
steps.memory_tip: Carbohydrate exactly one, fat below one, organic acid above one.

steps.label: The worked example
steps.margin_note: Equation, then the division, then the value. Three lines and the mark is safe.
lines: The value is less than 1, as expected for a
steps.why: The equation itself shows why: 80 oxygen molecules are needed to produce only 57 carbon dioxide molecules, so the ratio must fall below one.
common_mistakes: Writing the ratio as 80/57. CO2 goes on TOP, so it is 57/80.
Giving the answer without the equation. The coefficients are where the ratio comes from.
steps.memory_tip: Fifty-seven out, eighty in: the fraction has to be less than one.

steps.label: Why it never exceeds one for fats
steps.margin_note: One reason in four lines. The oxygen content of the molecule is the whole explanation.

lines.text: A fat is poor in oxygen, so it needs more

lines: A fat molecule contains very little oxygen of
So more atmospheric oxygen must be taken in to
The denominator is large, so RQ for fats is
steps.why: The reason is in the molecule: the less oxygen a food already contains, the more must be supplied, and the smaller the ratio becomes.
common_mistakes: Giving no reason. The last mark is for WHY, not for the value.
Saying fats release less carbon dioxide. They release plenty; they just need much more oxygen to do it.
steps.memory_tip: Less oxygen in the food means more oxygen from the air, so a smaller ratio.
